title: Paparazzi airborne architecture - derived example requirements
coverage: Covers the common airborne hierarchy, MCU0/MCU1 process and hardware boundaries, task sets, modeled connections and all four scheduling variants.
The four configurations are alternatives within one case, not four independent requirement datasets.
limitations: These are source-derived architectural requirements, not executable control laws or a claim of validation. Existing OSATE validation is not a pass.
The source declares modes without transitions and leaves several task inputs/behavior bodies unimplemented; no transition guards, servo algorithms, sensor processing or failsafe actions are invented.
The imported source references historical C files; those references are not proof that matching C bodies are present.

Paper table 2 gives radio-control/stabilization/inter-MCU-send frequencies of 40/20/20 Hz, while this fixed model uses periods of 100/100/250 ms. This draft follows the model snapshot and does not merge the paper timing table.
The original AADLib source has historical linking/type issues and a GPL provenance comment despite its repository-level BSD-3-Clause license; this draft does not relicense the imported source.
original_requirement_status: A publisher-hosted PapaBench paper and explicit PapaBench v0.4 provenance were located. No standalone original requirement set matching all four revised AADLib configurations was established.

source_search_evidence.title: PapaBench: a Free Real-Time Benchmark (WCET 2006)
source_search_evidence.finding: Read the six-page publisher PDF; pp. 1-2 describe the airborne split, p. 3 gives task-frequency tables and mode/precedence discussion. Historical design evidence; timing differs from this snapshot.

requirements.text: The example shall model one airborne system containing two separate subsystems: an autopilot (MCU0) and a fly-by-wire controller (MCU1), connected to one SPI bus. The ground station is outside the modeled system boundary.

evidence.note: Active model declarations; requirements describe this snapshot, not an independently validated flight implementation.

requirements.text: The airborne boundary shall accept radio-control event-data input and forward it to MCU1; MCU1 shall expose an outgoing inter-MCU message channel to MCU0, and MCU0 shall expose a return event-data channel to MCU1.
